title: Is brain size related to intelligence?
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explore whether brain size relates to intelligence. They cover genetics of brain size (twin studies, beta-catenin and ASPM genes, the EMX2 gene and cortical subdivisions), microcephaly and autism links to brain growth, ADHD and brain shrinkage with age, the encephalization quotient (EQ) and its limits across species, the controversial 2005 Michael McDaniel sex-difference study and its SAT-to-IQ conversion, Einstein's brain, the "tether hypothesis" on neuron connectivity, neurotransmitter complexity, animal intelligence comparisons (dolphins, octopuses), the city mice vs. country mice study, a German pornography and brain volume study, and a listener mail request for support for a fan whose wife has breast cancer during pregnancy. The hosts conclude there is no definitive answer.

segments.title: Introduction and framing the question
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode on whether a bigger brain means a smarter person, noting the evidence is conflicting and there is no definitive answer, with some banter about Branson and brain plasticity.

segments.title: Brain size across species and the encephalization idea
segments.summary: Brain size correlates with intelligence only to a point. The sperm whale has a larger brain than humans, but humans are not the largest-brained animal, so attention shifts to brain size relative to body size.
topics: brain size relative to body size

segments.title: Genetics of brain size: twins and specific genes
segments.summary: Twin studies suggest genetics influences brain size, with identical twins more correlated than fraternal. Beta-catenin controls brain growth in mice, where injected mice had larger brains and higher cognitive function but many died. ASPM is linked to microcephaly.

segments.title: EMX2 gene and cortical subdivisions
segments.summary: The EMX2 gene affects growth of functional cortical subdivisions tied to sensory input and motor output. Too little or too much expression hurts behavioral performance, so the gene appears finely tuned, as with baseball ability.

segments.title: Brain growth, autism, ADHD, and shrinkage with age
segments.summary: Rapid disproportionate early brain growth has been linked to autism. Adolescents with ADHD have brains about three to four percent smaller. Brains shrink with age, but loss of function is attributed more to protein buildup at synapses than to size, and sleep appears to clear waste from the brain.

segments.title: Measuring brain size, IQ, and encephalization quotient
segments.summary: Measurement methods vary (tape measure, body-size proportion, encephalization quotient), and intelligence measures such as IQ tests are questioned. EQ works reasonably well comparing mammals but less well beyond them. Human brains are about three percent of body weight but use a large share of energy.

segments.title: Einstein's brain, sex differences, and the McDaniel study
segments.summary: Einstein's brain was reportedly the same overall size but had some larger regions. Michael McDaniel's 2005 study claimed men are smarter than women based on brain size and converted SAT scores to IQ, a method the hosts find dubious. Scientists have called brain-size-intelligence links within humans pseudoscience like phrenology.

segments.title: Tether hypothesis, neurotransmitters, and animal cognition
segments.summary: The Harvard tether hypothesis proposes that early brains had tightly tethered neurons that were loosened as brains grew, enabling new connections. A competing view emphasizes neurotransmitter chemistry and complexity. The hosts argue that comparing dolphin or octopus intellect to human intellect is futile.

segments.title: Project Enigma, city vs. country mice, and pornography study
segments.summary: Project Enigma found a single gene mutation associated with brain size and IQ. A study of city and country mice and voles claimed urban rodents had larger brains, but only two of ten species showed this. A German study of three subjects suggested pornography use correlated with smaller striatum volume, with causation unclear.

segments.title: Discussion of Silicon Valley and Idiocracy
segments.summary: Brief tangent about the show Silicon Valley and the film Idiocracy, which the hosts say is frequently referenced on the show.

segments.title: Listener mail: help for a fan in need
segments.summary: A listener expecting a first child and whose wife has stage four breast cancer asks listeners to follow their tumblr, sponsor a 150-mile bike ride for fundraising, and give a shout-out to his wife, nicknamed the mayor. The hosts agree to help.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener, wish the family well, and give contact information for Twitter, Facebook, email, and the website.
